depth.display: 1478 m (4850-foot level); sources round this to about 1500 m
depth.locator: page 'The MAJORANA Demonstrator Project at the 4850 Level Davis Campus', paragraph on the shield and the underground location (the page states the level and its metric value)
depth.note: The 4850 Level is named for its depth in feet: 4850 ft x 0.3048 m/ft = 1478.3 m, the figure SURF itself gives ('4850 Level (1478 m)') and the one the local map uses. SURF's scientific director rounds it to 1500 m in the Snowmass 2022 paper ("campuses at the 4850-foot level (1500 m, 4300 m.w.e.)"); the same author gives 1490 m in a 2024 paper, and DUNE TDR Vol. I says "approximately 1.5 km underground". The water-equivalent overburden is the separate 4300 m.w.e. value. The far-detector caverns are on the 4850 Level. CHANGED 2026-10-25: was value 1500 m, display "1500 m of rock" (the Snowmass 2022 rounding), which disagreed with the 1478 m of the map level. Placement of the DUNE far detector at this level: DUNE TDR Vol. I, §1.1.2 and Fig. 1.4 (arXiv PDF p. 25): "the SURF underground area, also referred to as the 4850 (foot) level or 4850L"; ProtoDUNE-SP paper (arXiv:2007.06722, PDF p. 12): "a far detector located at the 4850 ft level of Sanford Underground Research Facility (SURF)". The quote above is SURF's statement for the 4850 Level itself.
depth.quote: The entire experiment will be located at the 4850 Level (1478 m) Davis Campus at the Sanford Lab Underground Research Facility (SURF).

name: SURF 4850 Level — LBNF/DUNE far detector caverns
notes: Coordinates unresolved to detector precision; see the coordinates note.

summary.plain: Caverns nearly a mile underground at the Sanford laboratory, excavated to hold the huge liquid-argon detectors of the DUNE experiment.
summary.technical: LBNF far-site campus on the 4850-foot level of SURF: two detector caverns and a central utility cavern, at 1478 m below the surface (the 4850 Level; sources round this to about 1500 m), 4300 m.w.e. overburden, hosting the DUNE far detector modules.
